skill.displayName: Pet Adaptive Drying Temperature Recommendation | 宠物烘干温度自适应推荐

version.changelog:
- Initial release of "smyx-adaptive-pet-drying-temperature-analysis" skill.
- Supports pet breed/type and fur density analysis from full-body pet images or videos.
- Outputs personalized drying temperature curves and time recommendations for safer pet care.
- Enforces strict open-id retrieval and API usage policies for report generation and query.
- Automatically generates Markdown tables for historical report listings with direct report links.
- Includes detailed usage instructions and safety guidelines for drying diverse pet types.

llm.summary: This skill mostly presents as a pet drying assistant, but it includes account-linked cloud history, token storage, unrelated health-style analysis code, and broad record-management actions that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is pet breed/fur analysis and drying-temperature recommendations, but the artifacts also include generic video analysis, health/constitution response handling, report export through a health endpoint, history listing, and generic add/edit/delete/page methods.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL instructions disclose remote analysis and open-id use, but trigger broadly on pet media, auto-save uploads, force cloud history lookup for history keywords, and do not clearly scope consent, retention, or confirmation for uploads, URL processing, or history access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No obfuscated or privileged installer was found, but the bundled requirements are broad and include questionable or nonstandard packages such as yaml and unattended-upgrades; the static raw-IP finding is limited to a dev config rather than the active prod config.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Remote media processing is expected for this service, but silent phone/open-id login or registration, payment-upgrade prompts, reusable auth headers, and public URL submission are disproportionate and under-disclosed for a narrow pet grooming recommendation skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The common utility creates a local SQLite user store containing profile fields plus token/open_token values, reuses those tokens for API calls, exposes cloud report history/export URLs, and includes delete-by-cameraSn methods without clear user-facing scoping or confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet media, URLs, and user-linked identifiers to this provider and having account tokens/profile data stored locally. Before general use, the publisher should remove unrelated health/generic/admin code, narrow the API surface, document retention and credential handling, and require clear confirmation for uploads, history access, account creation, and any destructive action.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in substance: artifact review confirms history/report listing, generic record-management wrappers, and generic analysis paths beyond the advertised pet drying recommendation workflow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the artifacts include destructive delete-by-cameraSn methods, account login/registration behavior, local token/profile persistence, and health-style outputs that are not proportionate to the stated purpose.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: nested API documentation and CLI text describe generic video or face/health analysis rather than the pet drying-temperature contract, creating a real capability/documentation mismatch.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partially accepted: broad default triggering on pet image/video requests is risky because the skill can upload media and query cloud history; a narrower explicit drying-analysis trigger would better fit the authority requested.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media upload/API processing is expected for this kind of cloud analysis, but the artifacts under-disclose local saving, URL fetching, credential handling, retention, and account-linked report history.
[AST7] unexpected: Downgraded: dynamic ORM attribute filtering is a code-quality/security concern in the generic DAO, but it is not the primary basis for the verdict because the larger issue is unnecessary generic persistence and token storage.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: Downgraded to contextual risk: the raw private-IP endpoint appears in a development config while the active configuration points to public service URLs, so it does not drive the final verdict by itself.
